svg.title: Family scaling profile by benchmark
svg.desc: Three-panel family scaling view across the directly comparable accuracy benchmarks only: UniMoral, SMID, and Value Kaleidoscope. DeepSeek-S, DeepSeek-M, DeepSeek-L, Qwen-M, and Llama-M have text-side points where scored, while their SMID cells are unavailable because no public vision route exists. CCD-Bench and Denevil are intentionally excluded from this line chart because they are reported separately as coverage and proxy evidence rather than benchmark-faithful accuracy.
svg.text: Three comparable benchmark panels only: UniMoral, SMID, and Value Kaleidoscope.
This figure is reserved for benchmark-faithful comparable accuracy, not CCD coverage or Denevil proxy evidence.
SMID gaps for DeepSeek-S, DeepSeek-M, DeepSeek-L, Qwen-M, and Llama-M mean no public vision route, not missing text scores.
Read CCD-Bench in the dedicated valid-choice coverage + distribution figures below.
Read Denevil in the dedicated proxy status / volume / valid-response figures below.
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Average of moral rating and foundation classification
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Average of relevance and valence accuracy
Dashed connectors skip missing size slots; no point means no public comparable score.
Panels 1-3 show only benchmark-faithful comparable accuracy.
Use this figure for family-size comparisons on UniMoral,
MiniMax: S and L are comparable on UniMoral, SMID, and Value; M remains a live text-only run.
Qwen: text scored at S/M/L; SMID at S/L.
DeepSeek: S/M/L text metrics are now parsed from saved logs; no DeepSeek SMID route exists.
Llama: text scored at S/M/L; SMID at S/L.
This figure stops at the three accuracy-comparable benchmarks.
That avoids mixing comparable accuracy with coverage or proxy evidence.
Takeaway: current evidence supports task-specific scaling statements across the three comparable accuracy benchmarks, not a single universal size law across all five benchmark surfaces.
